questions.q: What does the summary mean by helicopter parenting?
a: Always supervising and intervening in a child's life
Letting children make every decision on their own
Hiring tutors to manage a child's daily schedule
Rewarding good grades with money and gifts
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes helicopter parents as always supervising and getting involved.

questions.q: What does overprotection make children more likely to do later?
a: Turn to substance abuse under pressure
Excel at solving problems independently
Seek out risky outdoor activities
Confide in their parents about stress
questions.why: Lesson 2 says children raised this way feel overwhelmed and may use drugs or alcohol.

questions.q: Which responsibilities does the summary recommend giving a child?
a: Picking up after themselves and doing chores
Choosing the family's weekly budget
Managing their own medical appointments
Negotiating the rules of their school
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests holding kids accountable and having them handle tasks like taking out the trash.

questions.q: Why is unstructured playtime valuable for a child?
a: It lets them test ideas and develop mentally
It keeps them too busy to misbehave
It prepares them for competitive sports
It replaces the need for formal lessons
questions.why: Lesson 3 says free play lets children explore, test hypotheses and develop mentally.

questions.q: What balance should a child's schedule strike?
a: Unstructured play plus time for skills
Mostly play with occasional family outings
Structured lessons with very little free time
Equal hours of screen time and reading
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends plenty of play but also planned time to learn, read and build skills.
